report.source_text: Progressive improvement of visual acuity and healing of vulvar ulcers were observed over the days following treatment initiation. Her estroprogestative pill was switched to a progestative-only pill owing to the risk of thrombosis associated with Behçet’s disease. The patient was discharged from hospital on day 4. Within 48 hours, a TNF blocking agent (intravenous infliximab 5 mg/kg/dose) was started. Visual acuity improved progressively. Infliximab was administered for a total of 4 months along with oral azathioprine up to 2 mg/kg/day. She will likely continue azathioprine for long-term maintenance, once corticosteroid tapering is completed. At the last visit, one and a half years after the initial symptoms, the patient had not experienced any relapse. At the last visit, Heidelberg SD-OCT (Fig. 3 right) showed atrophy of the macula. Besides, OCTA images remained unchanged, but the patient had recovered a vision of 1.0 (20/20) in both eyes.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A healthy 23-year-old female presented with vulvar pain, edema, small vulvar lesions, and fever. Initial suspicion of HSV-2 was ruled out by negative PCR for HSV, Chlamydia, Gonococcus, and negative serology for EBV, syphilis, and HIV. Four days later, her condition worsened with multiple painful genital ulcerations, dysuria, urinary retention, and persistent blurred vision. Ophthalmological examination revealed severe ocular involvement including bilateral parafoveolar microhemorrhages, whitish retinal lesions, superficial and deep microangiopathy, and focal ischemia. Based on these findings, a diagnosis of Behçet's disease was made. Treatment with intravenous methylprednisolone, oral prednisone, infliximab, and azathioprine was initiated, leading to progressive improvement of visual acuity and healing of vulvar ulcers. At 1.5-year follow-up, the patient had no relapse, recovered vision, but showed macular atrophy. Her estroprogestative pill was switched to a progestative-only pill due to the thrombosis risk associated with Behçet’s disease.
